chunks: 27. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris said; Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ali ibn Ismail, on the authority of al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, on the authority of more than one, on the authority of Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): "What is the proof of Allah over the servants?"
He (peace be upon him) answered: "They should say what they know, and refrain (stop) when they do not know."

key_terms.حُجَّةُ ٱللَّهِ: The proof or argument of Allah
key_terms.زُرَارَةَ: Zurarah ibn A'yan, a prominent companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the proof of Allah over the servants according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration from Imam al-Baqir to establish the epistemological foundation of Shia theology, distinguishing between definitive knowledge and the humility required in the face of the divine essence. This principle serves as a safeguard against anthropomorphism and baseless speculation (ta'wil), reinforcing the scholarly tradition of 'stopping' (wuquf) when certainty is absent. It highlights that the primary 'proof' (hujjah) for humanity is not merely belief, but the disciplined application of reason and the restraint of tongue in theological discourse.
